RagShortTexts: Following Durbe, Herkus Monte led the Great Prussian Uprising, besieging Teutonic redoubts.

Variants.Content: Spurred by victory at Durbe, the Great Prussian Uprising (1260–1274) erupted across all Baltic provinces. Led by Herkus Monte, a Natangian chieftain educated in Germany, the rebels utilized captured siege artillery and European field tactics to raze Teutonic outposts, leaving only Königsberg and Elbing besieged.
Monte was a nemesis forged by the Order's own schooling. Fluent in Latin, he turned European military doctrine against his former masters, restoring pagan altars in blood sacrifices.
Teutonic garrisons in Königsberg boiled leather horse harness for food. Only continuous seasonal crusades proclaimed by the Pope prevented the complete extermination of the Order in Prussia.
